title: HUD notification producers and stock toast presentation
status: Static research. No notification producer is exposed as a callable SDK adapter by this map.

script_binding.name: hud_notification
script_binding.argument: The first argument is a string atom resolved through a predefined enum lookup. An unknown value reaches the invalid-enum argument error path.
script_binding.deduplication: Existing records with the same 32-bit type suppress a new append. This helper has no mod-owner argument.
script_binding.result: The callback returns zero Lua values. No receipt, arbitrary message string or caller-controlled duration is forwarded to the append helper.
script_binding.scope: This predefined HUD notification path is distinct from the stock loot toast slots. Its limitations do not prove that every game notification producer has the same interface.

stock_toasts.message: The slot message and item labels consume translation fields; the message uses an HTML binding rather than a plain text node.
stock_toasts.visibility: The container is suppressed when notification HUD visibility is disabled, the toast queue is empty, or the player's hide-loot-notifications option is enabled.
stock_toasts.ownership: These slots are game-owned presentation state. Overwriting a slot or its models does not establish a separate mod-owned notification.
adapter_requirements: Trace the producer and normal update phase before constructing or modifying native queue records.
Establish arbitrary text handling, attribution, expiry, dismissal and cleanup without clearing or replacing game messages.
Preserve the feedback API's text-only contract when using a component that normally consumes rich localized HTML.
Do not acknowledge presentation solely because a model was assigned; respect hidden HUD state and renderer lifecycle.

native_sync.selection: Active lookup requires the requested kind in its category and a present active record. Sync additionally requires a present variant with tag zero. Population stops at the first item whose ready byte at +0xbd is zero; it does not skip that item and continue.
native_sync.message_source: Native string at item +0x28 when its length is nonzero, otherwise the string at +0x0. The item label uses the string at +0x0.
native_sync.text_contract: These writes establish native string facts. They do not establish literal display text: the stock message/item models expose localization translations.

localization.binding: The JavaScript localization binding passes locID to DataAPI.bindLocString; it does not pass a caller-supplied translation field. core_get reads the translation of an existing bound model.
localization.missing_key_behavior: After primary and secondary lookup miss, the original UTF8 identifier is converted to UTF16, cached, and converted back to UTF8 for output. This is a statically traced literal-text candidate for valid UTF8 absent from both tables, not gameplay-qualified arbitrary text support.
localization.getter_modes: Normal lookup can translate a matching existing key. The id setting exposes the identifier; idandloc combines identifier and lookup result. The getter returns borrowed binding or shared scratch storage.

fallback_cache.bounds: No practical capacity or periodic eviction was observed in the reviewed lookup/insertion paths. Resource replacement and manager destruction clear the cache; refresh frequency is not established. Nodes can additionally allocate out-of-line key/value storage.

adapter_requirements: Bound distinct missing keys as well as active message count and publication rate. Queue expiry does not reclaim localization cache entries.
Preserve valid UTF8, length limits and the plain-text contract at the HTML-bound message sink.
Define behavior for existing-key collisions and localization debug modes before promising literal text.
Do not clear the shared localization cache to implement mod unload or message dismissal.
Copy borrowed translation results before their binding or shared scratch lifetime ends.

native_request_queue.scope: A richer notification path than the predefined script binding. The loot synchronizer consumes active kind 5 with variant tag 0; the single-string variant 7 is not the loot-toast payload.
native_request_queue.producer_arguments: NotificationProcessRequests environment and mutable native request; scheduler-borrowed environment lifetime.
native_request_queue.ownership: Enqueue destructively moves native strings and vectors and clears source storage. Borrowed guest byte buffers do not satisfy this contract.

string_variant.meaning: Owns a native string. Whether this is display text, a localization key or another identifier is not established.

native_request_queue.limits: Reviewed category consumer caps pending requests at ten and applies additional per-kind limits. Categories are shared with game notifications; no mod-specific receipt or cancellation contract is established.
native_request_queue.scheduling: The atomic producer count is incremented before payload allocation and initialization. This does not establish safe concurrent enqueue from an arbitrary worker; the normal engine scheduling contract remains required.
remaining_gaps: Qualify the statically traced missing-key fallback for mod text: distinct-key budget, collision/debug-mode policy, and HTML escaping; then verify in-game presentation.
Establish native payload construction, allocator ownership and safe producer phase.
Establish mod attribution, coexistence, expiry, reload/unload cleanup and delivery receipts.

stock_panel_presentation.appearance: Static tutorial panels use a dark translucent background, a thin translucent light border and regular game typography. The dynamic tutorial toast additionally uses backdrop blur and transforms.
stock_panel_presentation.mod_component: CRML reuses the static panel classes with independently owned plain-text elements, content-sized geometry and reduced background opacity. It disables transitions and animations, and does not attach native tutorial bindings or actions.
stock_panel_presentation.verification: Class definitions inspected in the reviewed stylesheet. Browser tests cover cleanup and idle DOM behavior; they do not establish native renderer performance or visual quality.
